title: Tiered degradation: lazy kernel retry and KV eviction throttling
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: production tail cases show two distinct failure modes that create steep cost/latency tradeoffs: transient kernel OOMs or scheduling preemptions that could be recovered by a quick kernel retry, and mass KV-cache eviction storms triggered by synchronized long-context requests leading to repeated cold misses. This PR implements a tiered degradation strategy: 1) a lightweight "lazy kernel retry" fast-path that only re-invokes a compatible kernel on transient internal errors within the same request instead of immediately falling back to a lower-precision model; 2) an eviction throttler for the KV cache that rate-limits bulk eviction operations and staggers eviction windows to avoid concentrated cold-miss spikes. Changes are guarded by runtime flags and safe defaults so behavior is opt-in for Dedicated/Private until validated in canary. Checklist: [x] implement lazy kernel retry with backoff and probe; [x] add eviction throttler with per-pool tokens; [x] expose tuning knobs via config and Console; [x] add unit + integration tests; [x] benchmark end-to-end tail latency and token-cost impact; [x] doc changelog and rollout notes. Design notes: lazy kernel retry targets only errors marked as transient (OOM_HINT, SCHEDULE_PREEMPT, KERNEL_CRASH_TRANSIENT) and only retries kernels with identical numerical precision and compatible memory footprints; retry is limited to 1 attempt per request and uses a jittered 5-20ms scheduling slot to avoid thundering herd. If retry fails or kernel is incompatible, we fall back to the existing precision-degrade path. The KV eviction throttler introduces a token-bucket per-GPU-pool eviction gate; eviction requests consume tokens proportional to estimated bytes reclaimed; tokens replenish at a configurable rate. If tokens are exhausted, eviction requests are queued with exponential backoff and a lightweight admission check prevents eviction storms from queuing too many requests. Config knobs exposed: runtime.lazy_retry.enabled, runtime.lazy_retry.max_attempts, cache.eviction.token_rate, cache.eviction.bucket_size, cache.eviction.max_queue_ms. Backwards compatibility: disabled by default for hosted tier, enabled in canary nodes and Dedicated feature-flag. Performance: internal lab runs (BERT-like long-context workload + mixed chat) show 8-12% reduction in 95th/99th token latency in scenarios dominated by transient kernel failures, and 4-7% CPU/GPU token-cost improvement when eviction storms were previously causing repeated recomputation. Risk and safety: lazy retry can increase a small window of latency for requests that would have been better served by immediate precision downgrade; this is mitigated by the 1-attempt cap and conservative transient-error classification. The eviction throttler prevents cascading misses at the cost of delayed reclamation under memory pressure; we surface eviction pressure metrics to Console and add an emergency override that forces immediate eviction if realtime memory crosses a critical threshold. Testing: unit tests for retry decision logic and throttler token math, integration tests simulating kernel OOMs and synchronized full-length contexts, epidemiology-style load tests validating no increased burst error rates. Rollout: 1) canary on dedicated pool (5% traffic) with metrics dashboards added; 2) expand to low-latency customers after 2 weeks of stable metrics; 3) tenant opt-in for Hosted via Console toggle. Docs: added operational guidance and tuning suggestions in docs/ops/tiered_degradation.md. See release notes for user-visible flags and recommended values.

review_comments: Diego Morales (review): Overall approach looks sensible. Main concern is ensuring we don't regress tail variance by adding retry jitter; can we add a metric exposing retry-induced latency to track regressions?
Author (Asha): Added retry.metrics.lazy_retry_latency histogram and a retry_reason tag. Also added an opt-out per-tenant flag so high-Latency-sensitive customers can disable retry at tenant-level.

Evelyn Chen (review): Eviction throttler makes sense, but token math needs to account for partial reclamation when pinned pages can't be evicted. Please ensure we don't silently starve eviction under memory pressure.

Author (Asha): Adjusted token consumption to be a lower-bound estimate and added an emergency override that bypasses the throttle if free-memory < 6% for the pool. Added tests simulating pinned pages where token consumption falls short.
Samir Gupta (approval): Verified integration test results and benchmark numbers vs baseline. Approve after CI green and docs updated.
release_notes: Introduces a tiered degradation strategy that adds a conservative 'lazy kernel retry' for transient kernel failures and a KV cache eviction throttler to reduce cold-miss storms. Exposed runtime flags for tuning. Disabled by default on hosted; recommended canary rollout for Dedicated. See docs/ops/tiered_degradation.md for ops guidance.
notes_for_ops: Recommended conservative defaults: runtime.lazy_retry.enabled=true (canary), runtime.lazy_retry.max_attempts=1, cache.eviction.token_rate=5MB/s, cache.eviction.bucket_size=50MB, cache.eviction.max_queue_ms=5000. Monitor metrics: retry.metrics.lazy_retry_latency, cache.eviction.throttle_backpressure, cache.eviction.emergency_override_count.
testing_summary: Unit tests cover decision branches for transient errors and token math; integration tests simulate kernel OOM and coordinated long-context clients; stress runs in the benchmark lab show reduced 99th percentile latency in targeted failure modes. No increased error-rate observed in canary over 7 days.
rollout_plan: Canary: 5% Dedicated traffic for 7-14 days, monitor 95/99 latency and retry metrics. Gradual ramp to 25% then 100% for Dedicated. Hosted: opt-in via Console until validated.
tagline: Conservative fast-path retry plus KV eviction smoothing to reduce tail latency without forfeiting correctness
